description: This file defines an abstract base class 'TypeSpec' and several derived classes that model different types in a serialization type system. It includes representations for pointer types, reference types, array types, generic types, named types, assembly-qualified types, tuples, and literals, each with formatting capabilities.

classes.name: TypeSpec
classes.description: Abstract base class representing a type with a method for formatting its string representation.

classes.name: PointerTypeSpec
classes.description: Represents a pointer type, with an element type, and overrides ToString to display as 'ElementType*'.

classes.name: ReferenceTypeSpec
classes.description: Represents a reference type, with an element type, and overrides ToString to display as 'ElementType&'.

classes.name: ArrayTypeSpec
classes.description: Models an array type with element type and dimensions, displaying as 'ElementType[,]' with commas indicating dimensions.

classes.name: ConstructedGenericTypeSpec
classes.description: Represents a constructed generic type with an unconstructed type and type arguments, formatting as 'UnconstructedType[Arguments]'.

classes.name: NamedTypeSpec
classes.description: Models a named type, possibly with containing types for nested types, providing qualified name generation.

classes.name: AssemblyQualifiedTypeSpec
classes.description: Represents a type with optional assembly qualification, formatting accordingly.

classes.name: TupleTypeSpec
classes.description: Represents a tuple type with elements and arity, formatting as a parenthesized list.

classes.name: LiteralTypeSpec
classes.description: Represents a literal string value, formatted with quotes.

methods.name: Format
methods.description: Abstract method implemented by subclasses to return string representation of the type.

methods.name: ToString
methods.description: Overrides Object.ToString to provide specific string representations for each type class.

methods.name: GetNamespaceQualifiedName
methods.description: Generates a namespace-qualified name for nested types.
